NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday said the High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC), constituted to investigate violence during student protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in July, had received very few complaints from those affected by it.During the hearing, the panel told a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant that it had issued notices in 149 newspapers inviting complaints regarding the violence during a march to Parliament on July 20. However, it received very few complaints, either online or in physical form.It also informed the top court that it had issued another appeal inviting complaints on October 21.Following this, the bench, also comprisig Justice Joymalya Bagchi, observed that in the absence of sufficient material, the panel was currently unable to arrive at any finding. It gave the committe one month to submit an initial fact-finding report.The bench also directed that all petitions, videos and complaints related to the violence be forwarded to the committee, which was constituted by the top court under the chairmanship of retired Supreme Court judge R Subhash Reddy.The other members of the panel include former Punjab and Haryana high court Chief Justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi high court judge Shalinder Kaur, ex-CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP LR Bishnoi.The Supreme Court had constituted the committe in August to investigate allegations of violence against student protesters and police personnel during demonstrations at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country.The protests were organised to demand the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan following the NEET-UG paper leak in May. Jantar Mantar, Delhi's designated protest site at the time, emerged as the focal point of the demonstrations, which later spread to other parts of the country.Pradhan resigned on July 25, following which the protests came to an end.
Article Summary: The High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) was constituted to investigate violence during student protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in July. The panel told a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant that it had issued notices in 149 newspapers inviting complaints. However, it received very few complaints, either online or in physical form.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday refused to entertain Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan 's plea seeking bail in a fresh Enforcement Directorate (ED) case, transferring the matter to the Allahabad high court and asking the Chief Justice to list it before a division bench on November 16.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed Khan to approach the Allahabad high court.Khan, a 10-time MLA and former Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister, had moved the Supreme Court against his arrest by the ED on October 31, shortly after securing bail in the last of the 95 cases registered against him since the BJP came to power in Uttar Pradesh in 2017.Appearing for Khan, advocate Mohd Nizamuddin Pasha argued that the arrest in a 2019 case relating to alleged irregularities in land purchases for Jauhar University was illegal. He pointed out that the FIR was registered 13 years after the alleged transactions involving farmers.In his petition, the 78-year-old leader alleged that the timing and circumstances of his arrest reflected a “blatant illegality” and a “gross abuse of process”, claiming that criminal justice machinery was being used for political ends to keep an opposition leader behind bars ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Khan also sought interim bail by invoking the Supreme Court's powers under Article 142, citing his prolonged incarceration and deteriorating health.He claimed that he had been named in 95 criminal cases since 2017, including the ED case. While he has been acquitted in six cases and three others were closed, he has been convicted in six. The remaining 80 cases are pending trial.“The clear pattern that emerges is that whenever the Petitioner is about to be released, a fresh case is registered or revived, and he is sought to be kept behind bars,” he alleged.Khan further claimed that he was arrested from the gate of Rampur district jail without being provided an arrest memo or written grounds for his arrest. He said he had already been questioned by the ED in connection with the case while in custody and alleged that the arrest was politically motivated.
Article Summary: Azam Khan had moved the Supreme Court against his arrest by the ED on October 31. NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday held a state-level protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru, demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged manipulation of electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Video footage from the rally showed party workers enacting the arrest of Gyanesh Kumar as part of the demonstration.The protest, which began at 11 am and was scheduled to continue until 2 pm, was organised by the Congress, CPI(M), CPI, CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc and Samajwadi Party, along with other progressive parties, social organisations and student and youth groups involved in the anti-SIR agitation.The demonstration was presided over by Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) President BK Hariprasad.Multilingual film actor Prakash Raj, CPI(M) state secretary Prakash K, CPI state secretary Sathi Sundaresh, CPI(ML) Liberation state secretary Clifton D'Rozario, Forward Bloc president JR Shivashankar and Samajwadi Party president N Manjappa also participated in the protest.Representatives of various organisations, including Sarvodaya Karnataka, Eddelu Karnataka, the Federation of Dalit Organisations and the Republican Party of India, attended the rally. Police personnel were deployed in adequate numbers at Freedom Park to maintain security and manage the gathering.The protest was held as part of the INDIA bloc's wider agitation against the SIR exercise and its demand for the CEC's resignation. It follows a demonstration organised by the opposition alliance at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1.On Wednesday, Hariprasad said the Bengaluru rally was a continuation of the November 1 protest and that leaders of several INDIA bloc parties had agreed to participate."In continuation of the protest we had on November 1, the entire INDIA bloc alliance is organising a massive protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru. Tomorrow, we have requested all our district units to simultaneously hold protests against SIR and Gyanesh Kumar and demand his resignation," he said.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Ramdas Athawale on Wednesday claimed Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) MP Supriya Sule could get a berth in the Union Cabinet during its next expansion if her party joins the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA)."It would be a matter of joy if Sule joined the NDA. We would welcome her if she joins the alliance. She could be considered for a berth in the next Cabinet expansion," the minister, whose Republican Party of India (RPI) is an NDA constituent, told reporters in Thane.Athawale also said that NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar, Sule's father, could have become President of India had he joined the ruling alliance in 2019. He also pointed to the "good relations" between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Pawar." Ajit Pawar had appealed to Sharad Pawar to join the NDA, but he did not accept the offer," Athawale added, referring to Sharad Pawar's nephew Ajit Pawar, who died in a plane crash in January.In July 2023, Ajit Pawar split the then undivided NCP and joined the NDA. The Election Commission subsequently recognised Ajit's faction as the "real" NCP, while the Sharad Pawar-led faction was allotted the name Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar).At the time of Ajit Pawar's death, the two NCP factions were reportedly close to a merger, but the process was subsequently put on hold.Meanwhile, amid the ongoing debate over electronic voting machines (EVMs), Athawale expressed no objection to elections being conducted using ballot papers.Questioning the opposition's criticism of EVMs, he pointed out that the machines were not introduced by PM Modi.He further stated that if the NDA failed to win the 2029 general elections, it would congratulate Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and accept the people's "verdict ... without blaming EVMs".Athawale also expressed hope that drought-hit farmers in Maharashtra would receive financial assistance before Diwali.The Union minister further urged the Thane police to conduct an impartial probe into the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Pradeep Purnekar, emphasising that no injustice should be done in the matter.

Article Title: SC issues notice to Centre, poll body on blanket immunity to CEC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought a response from the Centre and the Election Commission over a plea challenging immunity to Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners from any legal action for any decision taken in the course of their duties.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohanna issued notice to the poll body and Centre on a petition filed by activist and lawyer Arun Kumar Agarwal.According to Bar and Bench, the plea challenges the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023."Despite the absence of such blanket immunity, the Election Commission of India has successfully conducted elections over several decades. This shows that the Commission can function effectively without granting its members blanket immunity from legal proceedings," the plea said."The objective of protecting Election Commissioners from vexatious proceedings can be achieved through less restrictive measures, such as safeguards against frivolous complaints and prior judicial scrutiny. Granting blanket immunity is therefore excessive and goes beyond what is necessary to protect the independence of the Election Commission," it added."The said section takes away every civil and criminal remedy against the CEC and ECs for their acts. A voter whose name is wrongly deleted from the electoral roll, a candidate prejudiced by a mala fide act, and any citizen aggrieved by corruption in the functioning of the Commission are left without a remedy," it further said.
Article Summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohanna issued notice to the poll body and Centre on a petition. The plea challenges the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

Article Title: ‘You could smell alcohol on his breath’: Rahul Gandhi targets Bhagwant Mann over drug menace

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday slammed Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann , accusing him of failing to tackle the state's drug problem and alleging that he used to smell of alcohol during their time together in Parliament.Addressing the party's 'Insaaf Rally' in Sangrur, Rahul also accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government of being controlled by leaders in Delhi and questioned its ability to curb drug abuse.Recalling his time in the Lok Sabha with the Punjab CM, Rahul said, “I was in the Lok Sabha with him. He (Punjab CM) used to sit with us and tell jokes, right there, sitting among us. By 11:00 am, you could smell alcohol on his breath.”He clarified that drinking was a personal choice but said the chief minister's conduct was relevant to the state's fight against substance abuse.“Now, I am not saying that Bhagwant Mann shouldn’t drink; that is his personal affair. If he chooses to drink, that is entirely his own business. But if you truly want to fight the menace of substance abuse, your Chief Minister cannot be under the influence every single evening. You need someone who will fight for Punjab, someone who genuinely feels the pain caused by drugs, someone who carries the pain of Punjab in his heart,” he said.Rahul further alleged that the Punjab government was being run from Delhi with AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Union home minister Amit Shah exercising influence over the state government.“People here need a govt that works for Punjab. When the Congress party comes to power, the govt of Punjab cannot be run from Delhi. Our party will run the Punjab government from within Punjab” he said.“Right now, however, the reins are held half by Amit Shah and half by Kejriwal, while Bhagwant Mann just sits there. Punjab is being governed from Delhi,” he added.Rahul also questioned Amit Shah's claim that the drug menace in Punjab would be eradicated within three years.“What timeline did they (Union HM Amit Shah) set for the drug issue?... Within three years? In three years, Amit Shah won’t even be the Home Minister anymore... My assessment is that this govt won’t even last a year. Anyway, Amit Shah claims he will eradicate the drug problem in three years,” he said.Recalling his earlier warnings about the spread of drugs in Punjab, Rahul said opposition parties including the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal had dismissed his concerns at the time.“Many years ago, when I first visited Punjab, I pointed out that the drug menace was spreading there. The opposition, the BJP, the Akali Dal, and others, claimed that Rahul Gandhi knew nothing about Punjab and that drugs were not spreading in the state,” he said.He argued that Punjab needed industries, factories and a strong agricultural sector to create opportunities for people, warning that a lack of economic opportunities could contribute to drug abuse and gangsterism.The Congress leader accused the AAP government of failing to deliver on its promise to eliminate drugs from the state.“The Aam Aadmi Party came to power, and you placed your trust in them, in Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party. They promised that they would eradicate the drug menace. I ask you: where have they eliminated it? From which corner of Punjab have they managed to remove drugs? They are simply incapable of eradicating this menace,” Rahul said.The Congress leader also referred to his challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a face-to-face debate, which he said he had issued a day earlier.“Yesterday, I challenged Narendra Modi to a face-to-face debate. He can make anyone he wants the judge for this debate. I guarantee the nation that Narendra Modi cannot sit before me," Rahul said."I can guarantee that within five minutes of the debate starting I will prove that Narendra Modi is a 'desh-drohi' and Donald Trump controls him,” he added.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann of failing to tackle the state's drug problem. He also accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government of being controlled by leaders in Delhi. The Congress leader also referred to his challenge to PM Narendra Modi for a face-to-face debate.

NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Thursday disposed of the anticipatory bail plea filed by Manipur Congress MP and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam in a sexual harassment case after Delhi Police informed it that there was no immediate plan to arrest him.In its fresh reply, Delhi Police told the court that it was not contemplating Akoijam's immediate arrest. However, it added that if any new developments necessitated his arrest, a seven-day notice would be served on him.The court directed that Akoijam be given physical notice and asked him to provide the names of two persons known to him. It also said that if he failed to cooperate with the investigation, the investigating officer would be at liberty to approach the court.The Inner Manipur MP had approached the court seeking anticipatory bail after an FIR was registered against him at Vasant Kunj North police station. The matter is currently under investigation.Earlier, on Tuesday, the court had issued notice to Delhi Police on Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea and directed that no coercive action be taken against him until November 5.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh had also asked the investigating officer to appear with the case file.The allegations emerged in May, when several female students filed complaints accusing Akoijam of sexual harassment. The complaints alleged that he invited students to his campus residence under the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to sexually harass them. Some students also alleged that he made obscene and inappropriate remarks during classes.JNU dismissed Akoijam in October following an internal inquiry. He, however, termed his dismissal a "witch hunt" and questioned the due process followed by the university. The Delhi High Court subsequently stayed JNU's termination order and listed the matter for further hearing in January 2027.
Article Summary: JNU professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam is accused of sexual harassment. Delhi court disposed of anticipatory bail plea filed by Manipur Congress MP. Article Title: 'Normalise, recognise and formalise': Nadda accuses Congress of opposing SIR to legitimise outsiders, destabilise country

NEW DELHI: Union health minister JP Nadda on Wednesday accused the Congress of opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists to protect outsiders whose support, he alleged, had helped the party remain in power for a long time.“BJP's Amit Shah favours 'detect, delete and deport'. And what does Congress say? What does INDIA bloc say? They say 'normalise, recognise and formalise',” Nadda said, addressing the 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' padyatra in Bhopal.The senior BJP leader said the Congress was attempting to undermine constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission , because it was unable to secure public support, PTI reported.Additionally, he alleged that the opposition wanted outsiders to be issued Aadhaar and ration cards and settled in the country so they could become voters.“These people who have come from outside, normalise them. Make Aadhaar cards for them, make ration cards for them, settle them down,” Nadda jibed at Congress.“Tell me, should we detect them or not? Should we deport them or not?” Nadda asked the public, urging it to “delete” the Congress and the INDIA bloc.The BJP leader accused the Congress of attempting to weaken the Election Commission, alleging that the party blamed the poll body whenever it lost elections.“Realising that the electorate is unlikely to grant them any space in the political landscape for the next 20 to 30 years, they have resorted to blaming the Election Commission,” he said.He also accused the Congress of adopting different positions depending on election results, claiming that the party praised Rahul Gandhi when it won in Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh but questioned the Election Commission when it lost.He said Booth Level Officers (BLOs) visiting households to facilitate voter registration reflected the strength of India's electoral system.“In many parts of the world, voters must go to an election office to register their names, whereas in India, a Booth Level Officer (BLO) goes door-to-door to facilitate voter registration, and this is the strength of the Election Commission,” Nadda said.Nadda alleged that the Congress had dismissed elected governments 90 times while in power and questioned its claims of being committed to protecting democracy.Recalling the Emergency imposed in 1975, he claimed that he had been arrested twice by the police while he was a student.Nadda further accused the Congress and the INDIA bloc of attempting to destabilise the country and undermine the credibility of its institutions.
Article Summary: JP Nadda accuses Congress of opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists. Article Title: Judge facing rape charge presides over Pocso court
Article Text:
SC seeks Allahabad HC's response to a rape complainant's plea to suspend a UP judge who has been chargesheeted for rape and heads a POCSO court.

NEW DELHI: Can a UP additional district judge, chargesheeted for rape by Delhi police for allegedly sexually exploiting a woman, head a Pocso court which decides criminal cases against persons accused of sexually assaulting minors? Supreme Court has agreed to examine this petition filed by the rape complainant.A bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice Monday on the petition and sought response from Allahabad high court on her plea for suspension of the senior judicial officer.Appearing for the petitioner, advocate Rakesh Kumar Singh told the bench that at least judicial work should be withdrawn from the judge, but the Allahabad HC had rejected her petition.The bench in a cryptic order said, "Issue notice, returnable on Dec 11."The petitioner had lodged an FIR at Mayur Vihar police station on Dec 8, 2022 accusing the judicial officer, whom she met on a matrimonial site, of making repeated false promises to marry to establish a physical relationship with her.Delhi Police in Jan 2023 sought permission from Allahabad HC to proceed against the judicial officer. Two months later, Delhi HC granted the judge interim protection from arrest but allowed police to continue the investigations, she said.Police later recorded her statement before a magistrate.Police in June 2023 sent a reminder to Allahabad HC for early decision on request to proceed in investigations against the judicial officer but were informed by the HC that a vigilance inquiry was already going on against him. In Oct 2024, the chief justice of Allahabad HC permitted investigations, and the HC directed the judicial officer to cooperate with the probe.In April 2025, Delhi police informed the Allahabad HC regarding proposal to file chargesheet against the judge and on May 5 last year, the chargesheet was filed against the additional district judge under Section 376 IPC (rape). In Nov last year, Delhi HC allowed the trial court to proceed with the chargesheet but continued the interim order protecting the judicial officer from arrest.On May 23, the chief metropolitan magistrate of Karkardooma courts in Delhi took cognisance of the chargesheet, leading the complainant to file a petition before Allahabad HC seeking suspension of the officer. She moved SC after HC declined her plea.
Article Summary: SC seeks Allahabad HC's response to a rape complainant's plea to suspend a UP judge who has been chargesheeted for rape and heads a POCSO court. The bench in a cryptic order said, "Issue notice, returnable on Dec 11."

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke, along with Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das, National Spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and Singer Vishal Dadlani during a protest seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter roll deletions at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park.

Journalist Roshie detained: Neha

TMC extends support to CJP

'We follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi': Dipke

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Team of lawyer comrades are in touch with them.But if any lawyer can be at the PS immediately, pls DM."Rosie is among the three female journalists who filed complaint alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest in the New Delhi area on October 3.The complants have been transferred to the Crime Branch at Kamla Market for further action.Delhi Police also detained several protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating over an alleged incident of sexual misconduct involving three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters alleged that they had been demonstrating since 6pm on Sunday, demanding registration of an FIR in the case. Police detained them around 7am on Monday following a clash, with protesters alleging they were treated poorly despite only seeking registration of an FIR. Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Derek O’Brien also extended support to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders as party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that multiple sources had warned that the three could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other equivalent provisions.“With you all the way 🪳🪳stay strong. ‘10 Oct poora desh aa raha hai…’,” O’Brien said in a post on X while replying to Dipke.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) or National Security Act (NSA).“If the Govt believes that the threat of UAPA, NSA or years behind bars will scare us into silence, it won’t,” Dipke said in a post on X, adding that the protesters were prepared to spend “months or years in jail” but would not back down from their campaign to “save democracy”.He further said that they follow the path shown by Mahatma Gandhi and continue to resist “peacefully and non-violently”, despite what he described as attempts by the state to intimidate them.The developments come amid the CJP-led campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protesters have been demanding accountability from chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the exercise and have announced further mobilisation on October 10 in Delhi.
Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacting to the claim said they would not be intimidated by the possibility of action under laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.

Article Title: Inebriated man held for pelting stones at police commissionerate
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A 50-year-old intoxicated man was arrested on Monday night for allegedly entering the police commissionerate premises in the Mill Corner area and pelting stones at the building, shattering its glass door and causing damage worth around Rs 50,000 to govt property.“The accused, identified as Chandrakant Vitthal Magre of Pethenagar in Bhausinghpura, was arrested soon after the incident,” said Begumpura police inspector Pravina Yadav.He was produced before the court on Tuesday and was remanded in one-day police custody.According to the complaint lodged by police head constable Nagnath Bhanudas Kendre, the accused allegedly threw stones at the commissionerate building without any apparent reason. “The impact shattered the glass panel of the entrance, resulting in damage to govt property,” the complaint said.Following the incident, the police guards present on duty rushed to the spot and nabbed him and found him to be inebriated. Sub-inspector Tupe is conducting further investigation to ascertain the circumstances that led to the incident.
Article Summary: A 50-year-old intoxicated man was arrested on Monday night for allegedly entering the police commissionerate premises and pelting stones at the building. Chandrakant Vitthal Magre of Pethenagar in Bhausinghpura, was arrested soon after the incident. He was produced before the court on Tuesday and was remanded in one-day police custody.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Cop placed under vacancy reserve over sexual harassment complaint
Article Text:
Tuticorin

:





An inspector in Tuticorin district has been placed under vacancy reserve following a sexual harassment complaint.The officer, identified as Innos Kumar, was attached to the Kulasekarapattinam police station.According to police sources, a woman from a neighbouring district had been working as a data entry operator within the police station.She lodged a complaint stating that the inspector had allegedly sent sexually inappropriate WhatsApp messages during late-night hours with improper intentions.Based on her complaint, Tiruchendur DSP Mahesh Kumar conducted an inquiry and submitted a report to the superintendent of police, R Shiva Prasad, on Nov 1. Prasad recommended appropriate disciplinary proceedings against the inspector for his alleged act.Based on the report and recommendation, DIG, Tirunelveli range, R Thirunavukkarasu, ordered Kumar to be placed under vacancy reserve (VR) at the range office, Tirunelveli, with effect from Monday.
Article Summary: The officer, identified as Innos Kumar, was attached to the Kulasekarapattinam police station. The woman had been working as a data entry operator within the station. She lodged a complaint stating that the inspector had allegedly sent sexually inappropriate WhatsApp messages during late-night hours with improper intentions.

Article Title: Madapuram temple guard custodial death: Madras HC dismisses pleas of 4 cops, sets 9-month trial deadline
Article Text:
Madras HC





MADURAI: The Madras high court on Wednesday directed the trial court to complete the trial within nine months in the case relating to the custodial death of Madapuram temple security guard B Ajith Kumar in Thiruppuvanam, Sivaganga district, in 2025.Justice P Murugan dismissed petitions filed by four police personnel — then Manamadurai DSP Shanmugasundaram, then Thiruppuvanam inspector of police Ramesh Kumar, then sub-inspector Sivakumar and then head constable Ilayaraja — challenging the court's order remanding them to judicial custody.According to the prosecution, Ajith Kumar, who worked as a security guard at the Batharakaliamman temple in Madapuram, died during custodial interrogation on June 28, 2025. Police had picked him up for questioning in connection with an alleged theft of gold jewellery from a car owned by Nikitha of Madurai district. She and her mother had visited the temple the previous day.The state government transferred the custodial death case and the connected jewellery theft case to the CBI, which arrested six police personnel — Prabhu, Kannan, Sankaramanikandan, Raja, Ananth and Ramachandran, the driver of the van in which Ajith Kumar was transported.Initially, the CBI filed its final report before the fifth additional district and sessions court in Madurai against six police personnel. Subsequently, it filed a supplementary chargesheet naming four more police personnel — then Manamadurai DSP Shanmugasundaram, then Thiruppuvanam inspector of police Ramesh Kumar, then sub-inspector Sivakumar and then head constable Ilayaraja — as accused in the case, in addition to the six personnel already arrested.
Article Summary: B Ajith Kumar died during custodial interrogation on June 28, 2025. Police had picked him up for questioning in connection with an alleged theft of gold jewellery from a car owned by Nikitha of Madurai district. The state government transferred the custodial death case and the connected jewellery theft case to the CBI.

Article Title: Activist Mugilan arrested for non-appearance In jallikattu case hearings
Article Text:
Madurai

:





Cleared/270 WordsMadurai district CB-CID Madurai police have arrested environmental activist R S Mugilan at Erode on Monday night for not appearing before the court for a hearing in a jallikattu case registered against him. Later, he was granted bail on health grounds.According to sources, Mugilan hasn't appeared for hearings for the past three months, citing medical reasons. Subsequently, a non-bailable warrant was issued against him. He was arrested at Erode.He was produced before a judicial magistrate in Madurai; after Mugilan cited health reasons for non-appearance for hearing, he was released on bail by the magistrate.Speaking to reporters after appearing before the court, Mugilan alleged that he was illegally detained despite informing the authorities about his medical condition.“A case registered against four of us in connection with the jallikattu protest held in Madurai in 2017 is currently under trial. I have been undergoing medical treatment for the past three months due to health issues and was therefore unable to appear before the court. I had informed the CB-CID police about my health condition and told them that I would appear before the court during the next hearing and seek cancellation of the warrant.However, while I was travelling on a road in Perundurai in Erode district, police intercepted and arrested me,” the activist said.He claimed that police did not allow him to inform anyone about his arrest. “Though I was detained around 9pm on Monday, the arrest memo was provided only on Tuesday morning. I was also denied permission to speak with my lawyers and was allowed to inform them only after a protest,” Mugilan said.
Article Summary: Environmental activist R S Mugilan was arrested at Erode on Monday night. Mugilan hasn't appeared for hearings for the past three months, citing medical reasons. A non-bailable warrant was issued against him. Later, he was granted bail on health grounds.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.

Article Title: Family alleges mental harassment by teachers lead to suicide of Class 10 student
Article Text:
Kasaragod

:





The family of a 15-year-old boy who died by suicide at Azhithala in Kasaragod has lodged a complaint against the school authority levelling allegations of mental harassment.The father of the class 10 student, who was found hanging in his bedroom on Nov 1, alleged that his son had remained in the staff room of the school from morning to evening as a disciplinary measure over his alleged relationship with a girl.The family submitted a complaint to Kanhangad DSP Anil Kumar seeking a detailed probe into the incident.According to the parents, the boy, a student at a school in Cheruvathur, experienced mental harassment from teachers. The parents also demanded an examination of the boy’s movements on Nov 1, as he left home in an autorickshaw and returned with slap marks on his face.They also sought to identify the autorickshaw driver and to examine his mobile phone, including calls and messages.Nileshwar Police has registered a case for unnatural death and has taken the boy’s mobile phone for scientific examination.
Article Summary: The 15-year-old was found hanging in his bedroom on Nov 1. His father alleged that his son had remained in the staff room of the school from morning to evening as a disciplinary measure over his alleged relationship with a girl. The family submitted a complaint to Kanhangad DSP Anil Kumar seeking a detailed probe.

Article Title: Man arrested for attempt to break open ATM, CDM in Thrissur
Article Text:
Thrissur

:





The police on Wednesday arrested a 30-year-old man in connection with the recent attempt to steal money from an ATM and a cash deposit machine (CDM) at the State Bank of India branch at Thoravu near Pudukkad by cutting open the machines.The arrested person is Jithin, a resident of Kottayi in Kallur village, Puthukkad.The incident happened in the early hours of Friday. Thrissur rural district police chief Mohammed Nadeem said the special investigation team constituted to probe the case was divided into several groups, which examined numerous CCTV recordings and conducted inquiries at various locations.“The accused was identified through scientific investigative methods and is currently being subjected to detailed interrogation,” Nadeem said.Jithin is also an accused in a separate assault case registered at Varantharappilly Police Station, he added.
Article Summary: The incident happened in the early hours of Friday. The arrested person is Jithin, a resident of Kottayi in Kallur village, Puthukkad. He is also an accused in a separate assault case registered at Varantharappilly.
